project.name: ree-v3
project.description: REE V3 is the active implementation substrate for the Reflective-Ethical Engine (REE), a research programme where architectural claims become experiments over predictive-context, self-relevant forward modelling, harm modelling, commitment and offline integration systems. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: e2_world_uncertainty.py
nodes.summary: SD-063 E2 conditional predictive-uncertainty head over (z_world, action): a distribution-free quantile network with online pinball-loss training, replay buffer, and predictive std / variance readouts that feed ARC-016's dynamic commit-precision gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Quantile/HL-Gauss / pinball design with online mini-batch training, careful CPU-only Adam construction on first use to avoid pre-move device drift.

nodes.name: E2WorldUncertaintyConfig
nodes.summary: Config dataclass for E2WorldUncertaintyHead: master switch, network dimensions, quantile levels, online training knobs (learning rate, replay capacity, batch size), and readiness threshold.

nodes.name: E2WorldUncertaintyHead
nodes.summary: SD-063 quantile head: MLP trunk producing per-dim quantile logits over configurable levels, pinball-loss training on a rolling replay buffer of (z_world_prev, action, z_world_next) triples, and predictive-std / variance readouts scored against ARC-016 precision floors for E3.

nodes.name: forward
nodes.summary: Runs the trunk MLP on the concatenated (z_world, action) input and reshapes the output into [B, z_world_dim, Q] quantile logits.

nodes.name: compute_loss
nodes.summary: Standard pinball / quantile-regression loss: max(lv*err, (lv-1)*err) averaged over batch, dims, and quantile levels for the predicted vs realised next z_world.

nodes.name: _ensure_optimizer
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the CPU-only Adam optimiser at first training-step invocation, avoiding stale parameter references after device moves.

nodes.name: train_step
nodes.summary: One online SGD step on a single (z_world_prev, action, z_world_next) triple: shape/dtype normalisation, pinball forward+backward, optimiser step, training counter increment.

nodes.name: observe_transition
nodes.summary: Appends a detached (z_prev, a, z_next) triple to the rolling replay buffer, then draws a mini-batch and runs one train_step; consulted from the agent's E2 tick.

nodes.name: get_state
nodes.summary: Returns a diagnostics dict (train step count, observed transitions, replay capacity/size, readiness threshold, ready flag, quantile levels) for manifest logging.

nodes.name: predictive_std
nodes.summary: Reads the per-input predictive standard deviation as the sorted quantile IQR converted via a Gaussian-reference factor, averaged over dims.

nodes.name: predictive_variance
nodes.summary: Per-input predictive-variance readout (std^2, monotone rearranged for anti-crossing) with per-batch and per-dim diagnostics; the value ARC-016's dynamic commit-precision gate consumes.

nodes.summary: Process-S-style time-integrating running-sum accumulator of per-step waking demand used for the SD-SLEEP-ENTRY-PRESSURE entry-timing lever. Grows monotonically with waking steps; discharged on cycle completion so sustained sub-threshold demand crosses in bounded time.

nodes.name: MELConsumer

nodes.name: coalition_controller.py
nodes.summary: Core of the SD-091 coalition/topology control substrate: a non-trainable star-topology controller that opens typed control-demand coalitions from static templates, ticks them toward timeout or completion-condition dissolution, and exposes write_gate/channel_gain multipliers that consumer sites in the agent loop multiply into their existing signals.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic dataclass-based regulator (no nn.Module, no learned parameters); write gates are clamped attenuation-only (<= 1.0) while channel gains may exceed 1.0 -- a deliberate asymmetry documented in the SD-091 design.

nodes.name: coalition_templates.py
nodes.summary: Static COALITION_TEMPLATES registry mapping the two MVP-templated control-demand types (SENSORY_RESAMPLE, PROVENANCE_CHECK) to frozen recruit/suppress/channel-gain weight dictionaries over named consumer targets (E1 encoder, E2 forward model, hippocampal anchor set, BetaGate commitment sites, etc.), with placeholder magnitudes chosen to be numerically distinguishable at every site.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass template plus a module-level dict registry; the extensive docstring carries the target-name-to-module map that consumer wiring (SD-091 steps 4-5) follows.

nodes.name: control_demand.py
nodes.summary: Declares the 10-class MECH-481 typed control-demand taxonomy as the ControlDemandType enum, of which only SENSORY_RESAMPLE and PROVENANCE_CHECK are templated in the MVP; the other eight members are declared-but-untemplated pending their own consumer substrate.
nodes.languageNotes: Leaf module with zero imports -- the dependency root of the claustrum package.

nodes.name: CoalitionState
nodes.summary: Live state for one open coalition: per-target participating/suppressed weights (re-clamped to [0,1] in __post_init__) and channel gains, plus the per-request lifecycle fields (opened_tick, max_duration_ticks, completion_condition) consulted by coalition_gate and should_dissolve.

nodes.name: CoalitionControllerConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration dataclass for the controller: master enabled switch (default False, bit-identical off), the tuple of templated demand types allowed, the default coalition timeout in ticks, and the global channel-gain scale.

nodes.name: CoalitionController
nodes.summary: The star-topology coalition primitive: request_coalition() instantiates a CoalitionState from a COALITION_TEMPLATES entry, tick() dissolves timed-out or completed coalitions, and write_gate()/channel_gain() compose multipliers across all active coalitions for a named consumer target; recruited_targets/suppressed_targets expose the current topology and reset() clears state on episode boundaries.

nodes.name: CoalitionTemplate
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the static recruit (participating), suppress, and channel-gain weight dictionaries for one ControlDemandType; consumed by CoalitionController.request_coalition() to build a live CoalitionState, which re-validates the weights itself.

nodes.name: ControlDemandType
nodes.summary: Enum of the ten MECH-481 typed control-demand classes (e.g. sensory resample, provenance check, plus eight declared-but-untemplated members) that key coalition template lookup and the CoalitionController's types_enabled gating.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the REE preservation subsystem, re-exporting the ReconstructionRecord primitives, archive backends, and physical-token exporter that together make a REE organism reconstructable from birth inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel with an explicit __all__ covering all three submodules.

nodes.name: archive.py
nodes.summary: Content-addressed, append-only archive backends (local filesystem, S3-compatible object stores, multi-store replication) with optional client-side AES-256-GCM encryption for storing ReconstructionRecords durably.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazy imports of cryptography and boto3 keep top-level imports stdlib-only; object keys embed the record's sha256 hash, making stores append-only by construction.

nodes.name: reconstruction_record.py
nodes.summary: Defines ReconstructionRecord, an immutable integrity-hashed bundle of the exact inputs (config, seed, environment, provenance, understanding) that deterministically reproduce one REE life, plus faithful REEConfig JSON round-tripping and append-only file persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom dataclass serializer/deserializer preserves tuple-typed config fields that plain JSON would flatten to lists; integrity is a sha256 over canonical (sorted-key, compact-separator) JSON bytes.

nodes.name: token.py
nodes.summary: Physical-token exporter: writes an engravable ~180-byte key line, a gzipped full record, a manifest, a human-readable README, and an optional QR code so a preserved organism survives all-digital failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Stdlib-only at import time; the QR backend (segno or qrcode) is discovered lazily and is optional, with an injectable backend seam for tests.

nodes.name: NoEncryption
nodes.summary: Identity encryptor that stores plaintext JSON; the default Encryptor implementation.

nodes.name: AesGcmEncryptor
nodes.summary: Client-side AES-256-GCM encryptor with key generation, base64 env-var loading, and a nonce-prefixed ciphertext format so the object store only ever sees ciphertext.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports the cryptography package lazily inside the class so the module stays importable without it.

nodes.name: _BaseArchive
nodes.summary: Abstract archive base implementing content-addressed put/load/exists over the record's integrity hash, verifying integrity on both write and read and refusing to overwrite an existing key.

nodes.name: LocalArchive
nodes.summary: Filesystem archive backend writing records atomically (temp file + os.replace) under a local root directory; the hot copy that tests exercise.

nodes.name: S3Archive
nodes.summary: S3-compatible object-store archive backend (intended node 1: Hetzner Object Storage) with lazy boto3 client construction, injectable clients, and head_object-based existence checks.
nodes.languageNotes: boto3 is imported only when no client is injected, keeping ree_core import-light.

nodes.name: MultiArchive
nodes.summary: Replicating wrapper that puts a record into several archives and can verify a record loads with matching integrity from each backend.

nodes.name: s3_archive_from_env
nodes.summary: Factory building an S3Archive from a group-prefixed set of environment variables (endpoint, bucket, credentials), with an injectable client factory for tests.

nodes.name: IntegrityError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a record's integrity hash fails verification or is malformed.

nodes.name: RecordExistsError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when an append-only write would overwrite an already-stored record.

nodes.name: ReconstructionRecord
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass bundling record_id, seed, serialized config, environment spec, provenance, understanding, lifetime context, schema version, and the sha256 integrity hash of one REE life's birth inputs.

nodes.name: _import_dataclass
nodes.summary: Resolves a dotted ree_core-only path back to a dataclass type during deserialization, refusing anything outside the ree_core namespace.

nodes.name: _ser
nodes.summary: Recursive serializer converting nested dataclasses, tuples, lists, and dicts into JSON-safe structures while recording each dataclass's import path and tuple-ness for faithful round-tripping.

nodes.name: _de
nodes.summary: Recursive deserializer that rebuilds dataclasses and tuple-typed fields from the tagged JSON structures _ser produced.

nodes.name: config_to_dict
nodes.summary: Serializes an REEConfig into a plain JSON-safe dict via the recursive _ser encoder.

nodes.name: config_from_dict
nodes.summary: Rebuilds an REEConfig from its serialized dict, raising if the round-trip does not yield an REEConfig instance.

nodes.name: compute_integrity
nodes.summary: Computes the record's sha256 integrity hash over canonical JSON bytes of every field except the integrity field itself.

nodes.name: verify_integrity
nodes.summary: Returns whether a record's stored integrity string matches a freshly recomputed hash.

nodes.name: capture
nodes.summary: Builds a complete ReconstructionRecord from a live config, seed, environment spec, and caller-supplied provenance, asserting the config round-trips exactly before stamping the integrity hash.

nodes.name: reconstruct_config
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the original REEConfig from a stored record's serialized config dict, the read-side of birth-replay reconstruction.

nodes.name: to_json
nodes.summary: Serializes a ReconstructionRecord to a JSON string.

nodes.name: from_json
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON string back into a ReconstructionRecord dataclass.

nodes.name: write_record
nodes.summary: Persists a verified record to an archive directory atomically (temp file + os.replace), refusing to overwrite an existing record to preserve append-only semantics.

nodes.name: load_record
nodes.summary: Loads a record from disk and re-checks its integrity hash, raising IntegrityError on mismatch.

nodes.name: record_key_line
nodes.summary: Builds the ~180-byte engravable key line (scheme, id, seed, substrate commit, machine class, sha256) that locates and authenticates a record without containing its config.

nodes.name: parse_key_line
nodes.summary: Parses a pipe-delimited key line back into its field dict, validating the KEY_SCHEME prefix.

nodes.name: _default_qr_backend
nodes.summary: Lazily discovers an installed QR library (segno preferred, qrcode fallback) and returns a backend wrapper, or None so non-QR artifacts are still produced.

nodes.name: export_token
nodes.summary: Writes the full physical-token artifact set for a record into an output directory: key-line text, gzipped record, manifest with file hashes, README with verify/reconstruct instructions, and optional QR SVG/PNG.

nodes.name: _main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that loads a (possibly gzipped) record file, verifies its integrity, and exports the token artifact set, printing each written file.

nodes.name: blocked_agency.py
nodes.summary: MECH-353 blocked-agency / control-failure affect stream (z_block): a pure-arithmetic regulator that accumulates the 'assert/restore' pole when an intended action is repeatedly blocked by an external constraint while goal and capacity-belief are retained.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the assert-pole complement to REE's existing capacity-collapsed withdraw pole (SD-019b / z_harm_a). No nn.Module inheritance, no learned parameters — mirrors MECH-313/MECH-320/MECH-342 regulator pattern.

nodes.name: BlockedAgencyConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass configuration for the MECH-353 blocked-agency regulator (window size, attribution/capacity floors, output caps, gains).

nodes.name: BlockedAgencyOutput
nodes.summary: Per-tick output of the BlockedAgency regulator: assert pole, withdraw handoff, decommit signal, and diagnostic scalars.

nodes.name: BlockedAgency
nodes.summary: Pure-arithmetic MECH-353 regulator: integrates action-outcome comparator mismatch behind attribution and capacity gates, emits z_block assert pressure, withdraw handoff, and mid-execution de-commit signal.

nodes.name: stack.py
nodes.summary: Latent-space substrate: defines all encoders (world / self / harm streams / resource / goal) and the LatentStack composed module that anchors SD-005 z_self/z_world split, SD-010/SD-011 dual harm streams, SD-015 z_resource, and MECH-269 per-stream V_s.
nodes.languageNotes: PyTorch nn.Module subclasses; central to REE's split-latent architecture.

nodes.name: ReafferencePredictor
nodes.summary: SD-007/MECH-101 perspective-corrected world latent: predicts the reafference (self-motion contribution) to subtract from z_world, keyed on z_world_raw_prev.

nodes.name: HarmEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-010 sensory-discriminative harm encoder (A-delta analog): maps harm_obs → z_harm.

nodes.name: AffectiveHarmEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-011 affective harm encoder (C-fiber analog): maps EMA'd harm_obs_a plus optional harm history into z_harm_a with an auxiliary accumulated-harm head.

nodes.name: ResourceEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-015 z_resource encoder plus optional MECH-307 identity classifier head; feeds GoalState.update() for structured goal seeding.

nodes.name: HarmForwardModel
nodes.summary: Legacy harm-side forward model (deprecated in favour of ARC-033 E2HarmSForward); retained for parity with earlier experiments.

nodes.name: HarmForwardTrunk
nodes.summary: ARC-058 shared harm-forward trunk: modality-independent unsigned-PE substrate composed with per-stream HarmForwardHeads.

nodes.name: HarmForwardHead
nodes.summary: Per-stream signed-PE readout head that composes with HarmForwardTrunk under ARC-058.

nodes.name: ResidualHarmForward
nodes.summary: Residual-delta harm-forward architecture: predicts next-tick harm as z_harm + delta(z_harm, a); avoids identity collapse on autocorrelated signals.

nodes.name: HarmBridge
nodes.summary: Deprecated cross-stream bridge (z_world → z_harm); retained as legacy path — SD-011 supersedes.

nodes.name: _GradReverseFn
nodes.summary: Gradient-reverse autograd Function used by AdversarialSplitHead for adversarial split training.

nodes.name: AdversarialSplitHead
nodes.summary: Adversarial split head used by SplitEncoder to enforce z_self / z_world non-redundancy under the SD-005 split.

nodes.name: LatentState
nodes.summary: Container dataclass holding one tick of latent state (z_self, z_world, z_harm, z_harm_a, z_goal, z_beta, plus auxiliary fields for MECH-269 V_s, MECH-353 z_block, DR-13 self-recurrence diagnostics).

nodes.name: SplitEncoder
nodes.summary: Canonical SD-005 z_self/z_world split encoder: adversarial split with SD-018 resource-proximity head, SD-070 grounding heads, and MECH-451 residual-projection.

nodes.name: SharedDepthEncoder
nodes.summary: Shared depth trunk consumed by multiple downstream heads; a small MLP encoder utility class.

nodes.name: LatentStack
nodes.summary: The composed latent substrate: owns every encoder, runs encode() → LatentState, integrates SD-036 GABAergic decay, DR-13 self-recurrence, SD-018 proximity supervision, and SD-070 z_world P0 anti-collapse.

nodes.name: lateral_pfc_analog.py
nodes.summary: SD-033a lateral-PFC-analog: MECH-262 rule-selective persistence with mode-conditioned EMA update of a persistent rule_state, feeding an additive per-candidate score bias to E3.
nodes.languageNotes: First consumer of MECH-261 write-gate registry on SD-032a SalienceCoordinator.

nodes.name: LateralPFCConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass config for LateralPFCAnalog: rule dimensions, EMA update rate, bias scale, ARC-063 discriminator-source coupling, GAP-D trainable-head flag, and SD-082 readout-consumer knobs.

nodes.name: LateralPFCAnalog
nodes.summary: LateralPFCAnalog substrate: maintains a persistent rule_state EMA gated by MECH-261, sources rules from delta/world/CRF, and emits an additive [K] score-bias to E3; SD-082 amend adds centering + soft-tanh bound so a trained rule_bias_head can propagate through.

nodes.name: e1_deep.py
nodes.summary: E1 long-horizon predictor substrate: ContextMemory (a 16-slot cue-indexed context bank, MECH-152 substrate) plus E1DeepPredictor (LSTM transition model with SD-016 cue-context/action/terrain heads and MECH-216 schema readout).
nodes.languageNotes: ContextMemory holds the SD-016 cue-indexed retrieval + write-path substrate the 2026-08-19+ addressing-degeneracy amends operate on.

nodes.name: ContextMemory
nodes.summary: MECH-150/151/152 ContextMemory: a 16-slot key/value memory read by SD-016 cue-indexed attention and written by SD-016 read/write-path heads. Hosts the argmin/refractory/gumbel-learned write-selection modes and MECH-120 SHY normalise.

nodes.name: E1DeepPredictor
nodes.summary: Deep LSTM E1 long-horizon predictor: predicts long-horizon latent trajectories with SD-016 cue_action/cue_terrain heads, MECH-216 schema readout, MECH-482 epistemic-deficit consumer, SD-e1 action-conditioned transition (ITEM 1) and rollout-consistency (ITEM 2) knobs.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Coordinator HTTP service: pure-stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer + bearer-token auth exposing claim arbitration, chip ledger, heartbeat/status ingest, and manifest spool endpoints for the fleet's coordination plane.
nodes.languageNotes: Zero third-party deps by design (deploy target is a minimal CX22); the ingest boundary is the single place machine names are canonicalised.

nodes.name: Handler
nodes.summary: Massive BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass dispatching all POST/GET routes to db.py mutations; enforces bearer-token auth and MAX_BODY size on every request.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that initialises the DB and binds ThreadingHTTPServer to the WireGuard interface.

nodes.name: _canon
nodes.summary: Canonicalises a machine name at the ingest boundary; the sole place every mutable coordination key gets resolved so downstream tables never see raw hostnames.

nodes.name: load_tokens
nodes.summary: Loads the bearer-token to machine-label mapping from the JSON tokens file.

nodes.name: auth_machine
nodes.summary: Resolves an Authorization header to the machine label via constant-time hmac.compare_digest against the loaded token table.

nodes.name: _tc_open
nodes.summary: POST /task_claims/open handler wrapping db.try_open_task_claim; the ONE arbitrated claim entry point that returns owner or rival verdicts.

nodes.name: _tc_close
nodes.summary: POST /task_claims/close handler flipping a claim to done with closed_at + completion_note.

nodes.name: _tc_renew
nodes.summary: POST /task_claims/renew handler that refreshes claimed_at on a live claim.

nodes.name: _tc_amend
nodes.summary: POST /task_claims/amend handler for correcting a closed claim's completion_note while preserving completion_note_history.

nodes.name: _tc_dedupe
nodes.summary: POST /task_claims/dedupe handler removing byte-identical duplicate claim entries under one session_id.

nodes.name: _chip_record
nodes.summary: POST /chips/record handler creating a chip ledger entry from a spawn_task result.

nodes.name: _chip_claim
nodes.summary: POST /chips/claim handler that atomically claims a chip for a session so no other dispatcher starts the same work twice.

nodes.name: _chip_resolve
nodes.summary: POST /chips/resolve handler moving a chip to done/withdrawn/superseded with an audit note.

nodes.name: _chip_attach
nodes.summary: POST /chips/attach handler linking a spawn_task task_id to a pre-existing chip_ref entry.

nodes.name: _ws_append
nodes.summary: POST /workspace_state/append handler that submits a WORKSPACE_STATE.md Recent Work line via the DB pending queue.

nodes.name: _intent_replace
nodes.summary: POST /git_intents/replace handler recording a git commit intent used by the ree_commit sweep detector.

nodes.name: _dispatcher_lease
nodes.summary: POST /dispatcher/lease handler upserting the ree-cloud-4 metaworker orchestrator lease so the cloud-scaler holds the box up while chips are in flight.

nodes.name: _chip_episode
nodes.summary: POST /chip_episodes/record handler recording metaworker-run episode telemetry against a chip_ref.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: Coordinator SQLite layer: single-process writer with WAL + BEGIN IMMEDIATE around every claim guard, providing atomic claim/chip arbitration, experiment queue mirror, heartbeat/status ingest, and the pending-write queues the sync_daemon materialises into git.
nodes.languageNotes: Serial writer + connection-level BEGIN IMMEDIATE is what makes the claim atomic; the mutating verbs never rely on external mutexes.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: Initialises the coordinator database applying every schema migration in order (experiments, heartbeats, claims/chips, workspace_state, recommendation_log, IGW log, git intents, dispatcher_leases).

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens a SQLite connection in WAL mode with autocommit isolation and a 30 second busy timeout for the coordinator's single-writer discipline.

nodes.name: _migrate_task_claim_chip_tables
nodes.summary: Creates and evolves the task_claims and chips schemas including composite primary keys, lossless entry_json blobs, and per-verb index buckets used by every mutating claim/chip verb.

nodes.name: try_open_task_claim
nodes.summary: Atomically opens a claim under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, checking rival ownership for every declared file-shaped resource and returning owner/rival verdicts so the arbitration is server-serialised.

nodes.name: close_task_claim
nodes.summary: Flips a claim to done with completion_note and closed_at, refusing to guess when a session_id has multiple candidate claims.

nodes.name: renew_task_claim
nodes.summary: Refreshes claimed_at on an active claim while preserving its identity so stale-claim reapers don't confuse a live long-running session with an abandoned one.

nodes.name: amend_task_claim
nodes.summary: Replaces a closed claim's completion_note in place while archiving the prior text into completion_note_history so no correction silently erases the original claim.

nodes.name: record_chip
nodes.summary: Inserts a new chip ledger row for a spawn_task suggestion carrying title/tldr/prompt plus the chip_ref marker the spawned session self-reports through.

nodes.name: try_claim_chip
nodes.summary: Atomically claims a chip under BEGIN IMMEDIATE for a starting session so parallel dispatchers cannot start the same work twice.

nodes.name: resolve_chip
nodes.summary: Marks a chip done/withdrawn/superseded with note and confirmer verdict, closing the ledger entry for downstream materialisation.

nodes.name: record_chip_episode
nodes.summary: Persists a metaworker chip-episode telemetry row (start/end times, exit code, retry counts) against a chip_ref for the dispatcher observability plane.

nodes.name: upsert_experiment
nodes.summary: Reconciles one experiment_queue row into the coordinator DB mirror the sync_daemon derives from git, preserving claim state across reconciliations.

nodes.name: _claim_recoverable
nodes.summary: Predicate that says a stale claim is safe to reap either by six-hour timeout with no fresh heartbeat, or by machine-departure with the owner subsequently silent past COORDINATOR_CLAIM_REAP_QUIET_SECONDS.

nodes.name: claim_fence_active
nodes.summary: Detects an active claim fence on a given queue_id/machine pair so a rebooted worker cannot reclaim an item the coordinator has decided is fenced-off.

nodes.name: machine_departed
nodes.summary: Records a machine's shutdown notice (reason, timestamp) that feeds the departure-based claim recovery path.

nodes.name: claim_orphaned_by_departure
nodes.summary: Predicate that recognises a claim held by a machine that has announced its shutdown and stayed silent for the reap-quiet window.

nodes.name: try_claim
nodes.summary: Coordinator-authoritative worker claim path: conditional UPDATE under BEGIN IMMEDIATE that a runner POSTs against /claim, superseding the legacy git-push mutex.

nodes.name: evaluate_claim
nodes.summary: Non-mutating shadow evaluation of what the coordinator would return for a claim request, used by Phase-1 shadow monitoring to compare coordinator vs git verdicts.

nodes.name: release_claim
nodes.summary: Releases a worker's claim on a queue_id after successful completion or explicit release, mirroring the runner's own claim teardown.

nodes.name: record_result
nodes.summary: Inserts an experiment result row (outcome + manifest bytes) into the results table for the sync_daemon phase3_git_writer to materialise into REE_assembly evidence.

nodes.name: upsert_heartbeat
nodes.summary: Records a runner heartbeat row (state transition, machine identity, timestamp) that the state-change-only phase3_heartbeat_writer commits to origin.

nodes.name: record_status_payload
nodes.summary: Persists a runner /status payload for the live-status branch writer and the /shadow/status dashboard read path.

nodes.name: record_shutdown_notice
nodes.summary: Records a runner-announced shutdown reason (drain vs SIGTERM vs signal) so the reaper can tell process exit from machine departure.

nodes.name: insert_command
nodes.summary: Enqueues a remote-control command (stop/pause/kick/release_claim) targeted at a machine for the Phase 2 command-channel migration.

nodes.name: submit_workspace_state_entry
nodes.summary: Appends a pending WORKSPACE_STATE.md Recent Work entry into the coordinator-authoritative table the git materialiser drains at its next tick.

nodes.name: record_git_intent
nodes.summary: Persists the pre-commit intent record ree_commit.py writes so the pre-push hook can catch dropped-file sweeps.

nodes.name: upsert_dispatcher_lease
nodes.summary: Upserts the metaworker orchestrator's lease record so the cloud-scaler's HELD_BY_SELF invariant keeps ree-cloud-4 running while chips are in flight.

nodes.name: sync_daemon.py
nodes.summary: Sync daemon: Phase-1 shadow reads git and reconciles the coordinator DB; Phase-3 authoritative writers materialise result manifests, experiment queue snapshots, and heartbeat/status files from the DB into REE_assembly and ree-v3 as the sole git writer.
nodes.languageNotes: Phase-3 writers hold a per-repo mkdir-based rebase lock; the design is deliberately structurally incapable of the autostash-loss class the whole project exists to remove.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Daemon loop entry point that parses SYNC_MODE flags, opens the DB, and dispatches to reconcile_once and the three phase3 writers on their configured cadences.

nodes.name: reconcile_once
nodes.summary: One reconcile tick: fetches the authoritative git ref for experiment_queue.json and upserts each item into the coordinator DB mirror while preserving live claim state.

nodes.name: phase3_git_writer
nodes.summary: Sole git writer for result manifests: drains the pending spool into REE_assembly/evidence/experiments, commits with a phase3 prefix, pushes, and only marks committed_at on push success so a crash mid-write is idempotent-retryable.

nodes.name: phase3_queue_writer
nodes.summary: Sole git writer for experiment_queue.json: re-materialises the queue from the DB every tick, commits with a phase3-queue prefix, and self-heals rebase conflicts on the queue file via reset+rewrite.

nodes.name: phase3_heartbeat_writer
nodes.summary: State-change-only heartbeat writer: derives per-machine runner_heartbeats and runner_status JSON files from the DB and commits under phase3-heartbeats only when a machine's state actually transitions.

nodes.name: _sync_to_origin
nodes.summary: Shared rebase-and-push helper protected by an mkdir-based per-repo lock that push-retries under a bounded rebase window and refuses to touch the working tree on lock loss.

nodes.name: _materialize_runpacks
nodes.summary: Renders per-run manifest bytes into REE_assembly's runs/ pack layout that the evidence indexer consumes.

nodes.name: _materialize_sidefiles
nodes.summary: Writes auxiliary sidecar files (JSONL logs, per-run supplements) alongside the primary run pack under the same commit.

nodes.name: _quarantine_oversized_sidefile
nodes.summary: Diverts sidecar files above the size cap into a quarantine directory so a single oversized artifact cannot wedge the writer.

nodes.name: test_task_claim_chip_mutations.py
nodes.summary: Contract suite for the Phase-2 mutating verbs in db.py: real SQLite files + real threads to prove the BEGIN IMMEDIATE atomicity of every claim/chip verb, headlined by the 2026-07-28 three-session collision reproduction.

nodes.name: Base
nodes.summary: Shared TestCase base that materialises a real coordinator DB in a tempdir for each test so the mutation verbs run against genuine sqlite transactions.

nodes.name: TestOpen
nodes.summary: Contracts for try_open_task_claim including the flagship two-concurrent-opens-produce-exactly-one-owner test that replays the 2026-07-28 three-session collision under real threads.

nodes.name: TestCloseRenewAmend
nodes.summary: Contracts for close/renew/amend verifying completion_note_history preservation, ambiguous-close refusal, and the stale-threshold semantics.

nodes.name: TestChips
nodes.summary: Contracts for the chip ledger mutation verbs (record/claim/unclaim/resolve/attach/amend_prompt) including the atomic claim race and archived-field round-trip behaviour.

nodes.name: TestScopeGuards
nodes.summary: Contracts for directory-scope claim guards ensuring scope claims are exempt from arbitration exactly where the CLAUDE.md rule specifies.

nodes.name: _chip
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a fully-populated chip payload dict so the chip-verb tests stay compact and consistent.

nodes.name: e3_selector.py
nodes.summary: E3 trajectory selector implementing the substrate's action-selection loop with precision/authority arbitration, WCI floors, benefit/harm evaluation, ghost-goal integration, and residue-field integration — the primary policy stage that turns E2 fast predictions into committed actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large single-class module (E3TrajectorySelector spans ~4200 lines with 50 methods); pure PyTorch runtime with extensive config-driven feature flags.

nodes.name: SelectionResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass container for a single selection step's outputs: chosen trajectory index, per-candidate scores/logits, and diagnostic fields consumed by upstream instrumentation.

nodes.name: E3TrajectorySelector
nodes.summary: Central E3 policy module: consumes E2 candidate trajectories, applies precision/authority arbitration, WCI floors, benefit/harm heads, ghost-goal biases and residue-field pulls, then samples a committed action via the noisy selection head.
nodes.languageNotes: Monolithic torch.nn.Module with 50 methods covering precision recalibration, benefit/harm evaluation, WCI symmetric-RV floor, alignment biasing, and post-hoc calibration.

nodes.name: project_channel_range
nodes.summary: Projects a tensor of per-channel features into a normalised active range used by downstream authority-spread and commit-threshold computations.

nodes.name: authority_spread_ratio
nodes.summary: Computes the authority spread ratio between a candidate lever and the currently dominant one over a basis set — the core scalar arbitrating precision/authority competition in E3.

nodes.name: authority_ratio_is_competitive
nodes.summary: Threshold predicate over an authority spread ratio determining whether a challenger lever is competitive enough to trigger switching.

nodes.name: variance_commit_threshold
nodes.summary: Resolves the running-variance commit threshold from configuration, applying floors used by E3's commit gate.

nodes.name: compute_action_object_alignment_bias
nodes.summary: Computes a per-candidate additive bias that pulls E3 selection toward trajectories whose action agrees with the current action-object alignment signal, weighted per config.

nodes.name: schema.sql
nodes.summary: SQLite schema for the experiment coordinator (hub-side). Defines the authoritative tables for the experiment queue, run results, machine heartbeats/commands, claim audit, TASK_CLAIMS/TASK_CHIPS mirrors, drift audit, WORKSPACE_STATE/RECOMMENDATION_LOG/IGW append intake, dispatcher leases, and generic git-intent audit -- applied idempotently at coordinator startup.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLite pragmas (WAL journal, NORMAL sync, foreign_keys ON) and IF NOT EXISTS idempotence throughout so the file is safe to re-run at startup.

nodes.name: experiments
nodes.summary: Authoritative queue store: one row per experiment queue item, mirroring the validate_queue.py item schema. Records status/priority/machine affinity plus lossless item_json and terminal removal_reason/removed_at.

nodes.name: results
nodes.summary: One row per completed run keyed by run_id so result delivery is idempotent. Stores outcome, manifest bytes/sha, receive time, and the sync-daemon commit timestamp.

nodes.name: heartbeats
nodes.summary: Latest per-machine runner heartbeat plus separate machine-shutdown and process-exit columns so a runner exit cannot overwrite the scaler's fence-arming shutdown reason.

nodes.name: commands
nodes.summary: Pending and acked remote-control commands (pause/resume/stop/kick/release_claim). Pending == acked_at NULL; ack stamps result_status and result_note as an audit trail.

nodes.name: heartbeat_log
nodes.summary: Append-only heartbeat history keyed to state transitions (start/finish/switch/idle) rather than every tick, so it can answer 'what was machine X doing at time T' without unbounded growth. Trimmed to a retention window.

nodes.name: claim_log
nodes.summary: Shadow audit of claim attempts: one row per attempt comparing the git verdict to the coordinator's own verdict, with a diverged flag that gates advancing past Phase 1.

nodes.name: task_claims
nodes.summary: Mirror of TASK_CLAIMS.json claims[] entries with a composite (session_id, claimed_at) primary key. Carries status, completion note history, and the lossless original entry.

nodes.name: task_claim_resources
nodes.summary: Child table listing the resources (repo-relative paths) each task_claims row holds. FK cascades on delete; enables server-side rival lookup as a single indexed SELECT rather than a JSON scan.

nodes.name: chip_ledger
nodes.summary: Mirror of TASK_CHIPS.json chips[] entries keyed by chip_ref. Tracks spawn/claim/resolution lifecycle, host attribution, archived prompt/resolution fields, and lossless entry_json.

nodes.name: task_claim_chip_drift_log

nodes.name: workspace_state_entries
nodes.summary: Append-only spool for WORKSPACE_STATE.md entries. Clients POST /workspace_state/append; the materializer splices pending rows into the live file and stamps materialized_at once the text provably reached git.

nodes.name: recommendation_log_entries
nodes.summary: Append-only spool for RECOMMENDATION_LOG.jsonl. Same materialization contract as workspace_state_entries; each row is one exact jsonl line stamped once it reaches git.

nodes.name: dispatcher_leases

nodes.name: igw_log_entries

nodes.name: git_intent_log

nodes.name: zworld_p0.py
nodes.summary: SD-070 anti-collapse P0 training recipe for the z_world encoder: scene-structure supervision (hazard/resource presence + bucketed Chebyshev distance), class-balanced CE, VICReg variance/covariance penalty, optional resource-proximity, resource-field, and reconstruction heads, with held-out probe reporting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses torch.nn functional API with dataclass-based config; ZWorldP0Trainer stores buffered observations and constructs auxiliary heads on-the-fly during train().

nodes.name: chebyshev_offsets
nodes.summary: Builds a per-cell tensor of Chebyshev distances from the centre of a 5x5 local view, used to derive nearest-entity distance buckets.

nodes.name: entity_presence_mask
nodes.summary: Extracts a boolean 5x5 presence mask from world_obs for a given entity-type channel, handling both batched and unbatched inputs.

nodes.name: scene_structure_targets
nodes.summary: Derives hazard/resource presence labels and bucketed nearest-Chebyshev-distance labels from raw world_obs, forming the SD-070 grounding targets that supervise the anti-collapse P0 heads.

nodes.name: balanced_class_weights
nodes.summary: Computes inverse-frequency class weights over a label tensor, zeroing absent classes so the CE loss compensates for the ~95% class-0 saturation baseline.

nodes.name: variance_covariance_penalty
nodes.summary: VICReg-style regulariser: hinge on per-dim std to enforce variance above a threshold, plus mean squared off-diagonal covariance to prevent latent collapse of z_world onto a single effective dimension.

nodes.name: ZWorldP0Config
nodes.summary: Dataclass configuration for the SD-070 P0 trainer, covering loss weights (variance/covariance/presence/distance/proximity/resource-field/reconstruction), optimizer, batch size, epochs, seed, and holdout fraction.

nodes.name: ZWorldP0Trainer
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the SD-070 anti-collapse P0 training loop: buffers observations, builds classification/regression heads lazily, splits into train/holdout, runs Adam with grad clipping and VICReg penalty, and produces a diagnostic holdout report with per-target accuracy/recall and participation-ratio proxies.
nodes.languageNotes: Constructs auxiliary nn.Linear heads on-demand during train() so they persist across calls; uses torch.Generator for reproducible shuffling and batch sampling.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: Central REEAgent implementation that wires together predictors, PFC/PAG/hippocampal/claustrum modules, comparators, affect accumulators, latent stacks, and action-learning to run the full Reflective-Ethical Engine cognitive cycle (sense -> E1/E2/E3 predict -> select -> act) with actor-critic training and offline chunk replay.
nodes.languageNotes: Monolithic 12k-line Python class (REEAgent, 104 methods) that composes ~46 sibling ree_core modules; effectively the substrate's top-level integration surface.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: Lightweight dataclass holding the per-tick observable agent state (nine properties, no behaviour) passed to instrumentation and comparators.

nodes.name: REEAgent
nodes.summary: The Reflective-Ethical Engine agent: composes and drives every substrate module (E1 deep world model, E2 fast/harm/world predictors, E3 selector, PFC analogs, hippocampal/claustrum/PAG/amygdala modules, latent stacks, residue field, blocked-agency and harm-suffering accumulators, scientist attribution, coalition control, actor-critic policy) across sense/select/act ticks, offline sleep replay, and chunk/policy-decomposition state.
nodes.languageNotes: Extreme integration surface (104 methods); every V3 architectural mechanism eventually attaches here.

nodes.name: candidate_support_preflight
nodes.summary: Precomputes per-class support statistics (counts, entropy, absolute-value spread) over first-action candidates plus optional forced score biases, used to detect degenerate or collapsed candidate distributions before E3 scoring.

nodes.name: _resolve_chunk_deliberation_horizon
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective per-chunk deliberation horizon from an REE config, applying default and clamp rules for downstream chunk-replay bookkeeping.

nodes.name: REEAgent.__init__
nodes.summary: Constructs the REEAgent by instantiating and wiring every submodule (predictors, PFC analogs, hippocampal/claustrum modules, comparators, latent stacks, actor-critic head, buffers) from the resolved REEConfig.

nodes.name: REEAgent.from_config
nodes.summary: Class-method factory that builds an REEAgent from a raw config dict or REEConfig object, applying dimension inference and default resolution.

nodes.name: REEAgent.reset
nodes.summary: Clears per-episode state (buffers, latent stacks, comparator caches, exploration episodes) so the agent can begin a fresh environment episode without cross-contamination.

nodes.name: REEAgent.sense
nodes.summary: Ingests a structured observation into the perceptual pipeline (object-file buffer, latent stack, hippocampal/amygdala inputs), refreshing z_world and downstream comparator inputs for the coming decision tick.

nodes.name: REEAgent.sense_flat
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that accepts a flat observation tensor and routes it through the same sense pipeline used for structured observations.

nodes.name: REEAgent.generate_trajectories
nodes.summary: Rolls out candidate action trajectories through the E1/E2 forward models to seed E3 scoring and curiosity diagnostics for the current decision point.

nodes.name: REEAgent.select_action
nodes.summary: Runs the E3 selector over candidate trajectories with claustrum coalition control, PFC gating, and coalition/persistence biases to choose the action for the current tick.

nodes.name: REEAgent.act
nodes.summary: Top-level convenience wrapper that runs the full sense -> predict -> select -> commit -> record cycle for one environment step and returns the chosen action plus diagnostics.

nodes.name: REEAgent.actor_critic_step
nodes.summary: Performs one actor-critic training update over recent trajectories, backpropagating policy and value gradients through the E3 selector and encoder.

nodes.name: REEAgent.actor_critic_reward
nodes.summary: Ingests a scalar reward signal for the actor-critic head, buffering it against the pending decision for the next update.

nodes.name: REEAgent.notify_env_completion
nodes.summary: Signals an environment episode boundary so the agent can flush exploration episodes, close chunks, and trigger offline consolidation hooks.

nodes.name: REEAgent.notify_subgoal_attainment
nodes.summary: Informs the ghost-goal bank and PFC modules that a subgoal has been attained, updating goal-tracking state.

nodes.name: REEAgent.update_object_file_buffer
nodes.summary: Refreshes the object-file buffer with the current observation's entities so downstream attention and comparator modules see up-to-date object identity information.

nodes.name: REEAgent.note_chunk_outcome
nodes.summary: Records the outcome of a closed policy chunk into the chunking bookkeeping used by policy decomposition and offline replay.

nodes.name: REEAgent.note_chunk_replay_sequence
nodes.summary: Appends a replayed chunk sequence into the offline consolidation buffer for later sleep-phase integration.

nodes.name: REEAgent.get_chunking_state
nodes.summary: Exposes the current chunking state (open chunks, deliberation horizon, recent outcomes) for instrumentation and experiment logging.

nodes.name: REEAgent.get_policy_decomposition_state
nodes.summary: Returns the current policy-decomposition tree/state used by chunking and offline consolidation for external inspection.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central REE-v3 configuration substrate: 16 nested dataclasses (LatentStackConfig, E1/E2/E3Config, HippocampalConfig, ResidueConfig, HeartbeatConfig, EnvironmentConfig and the umbrella REEConfig) plus the from_dims factory that binds them into a single agent-wide config with post-init resolvers. Every experimental knob for SD/MECH/ARC substrates threads through this module's three-site pattern (field, from_dims signature, from_dims assignment).
nodes.languageNotes: Massive 10k-line dataclass hierarchy. REEConfig alone declares 710 fields with 7 methods (from_dims, __post_init__, enable_* preset resolvers). The 'silent-kwargs' hazard is well-known: a knob missing any of dataclass-field / from_dims-signature / from_dims-body assignment silently falls into **kwargs and is discarded (see [memory] reference-reeconfig-from-dims-silent-kwargs).

nodes.name: derive_stdlib_rng_seed
nodes.summary: Derives a distinct reproducible per-consumer seed from a base seed and stream id, so multiple stdlib-random consumers seeded from one base never draw correlated sequences. Passes None through so callers keep the process-global default when no seed is set.

nodes.name: _register_observed_config
nodes.summary: Registers a REEConfig instance into a module-level weakref registry so an experiment-side auditor can enumerate every config actually observed in a run (used by observability tooling to detect silent-kwargs drops and default-vs-explicit divergences).

nodes.name: LatentStackConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration dataclass for the V3 latent stack (L-space): dimensions for z_self/z_world/z_beta/z_theta/z_delta plus flags for SD-005 stream separation, SD-007 reafference correction, SD-010/011 harm-stream encoders, SD-018 resource-proximity supervision, and downstream latent-side substrates (SD-056 e2 contrastive, SD-063 uncertainty head, SD-070 P0 anti-collapse recipe).

nodes.name: E2Config
nodes.summary: E2 (fast forward model) configuration: world_forward / self_forward / action-object encoder dims plus SD-013 interventional training, SD-056 action-conditional divergence contrastive loss (incl. multi-step amend), and rollout output-norm clamp.

nodes.name: E3Config

nodes.name: REEConfig
nodes.summary: Umbrella agent-wide configuration binding every sub-config (LatentStack / E1 / E2 / E3 / EventSegmenter / Anchor / Ghost / Hippocampal / Residue / Heartbeat / Environment / goal.GoalConfig / serotonin.SerotoninConfig) plus a from_dims factory that surfaces the top-level knobs and re-runs __post_init__ preset resolvers (enable_goal_stream / enable_sleep_aggregation_cluster / OR-only master resolvers) after cls() so every from_dims caller lands the same effective config as direct construction.

The from_dims signature is the primary risk surface — a knob missing at any of the three sites (field, signature, assignment) falls into **kwargs silently. tour.title: The Agent Orchestrator
tour.description: REEAgent is the central loop that binds every V3 substrate together: it wires predictors (E1/E2/E3), the PFC/PAG/hippocampal/claustrum modules, comparators, affect accumulators, latent stacks, and action-learning into the full Reflective-Ethical Engine cognitive cycle (sense -> E1/E2/E3 predict -> select -> act). Start here to see how the pieces integrate; each of the following steps zooms into one module class this file instantiates.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses composed via kwargs let a single 'god object' remain readable when it aggregates many substrates. Look for how each subsystem is passed in through its own typed dataclass config, keeping construction wiring explicit and per-experiment toggle-able rather than hidden in mutable global state.

tour.title: The Substrate Config Registry
tour.description: REEConfig is the single dataclass-of-dataclasses that turns feature flags into a wired agent. The `from_dims` factory constructs 16 nested configs (LatentStackConfig, E1/E2/E3Config, HippocampalConfig, ResidueConfig, HeartbeatConfig, EnvironmentConfig, ...) with cross-checked post-init validators, so every experiment queue entry can knob one substrate on or off without touching agent wiring. This is the contract you edit when adding a new module or knob.
tour.languageLesson: Python's nested @dataclass pattern with __post_init__ acts as a light schema: defaults live near the fields, validation runs on construction, and factories like `from_dims` amount to a typed constructor -- much lighter than pydantic while still catching mis-wired experiments early.

tour.title: Environment and the Latent Stack
tour.description: CausalGridWorld is the ~5300-line gridworld substrate that emits observations through the InvariantTypes sensory/action interface. LatentStack composes all encoders (world / self / harm / resource / goal) and anchors the SD-005 z_self/z_world split, SD-010/SD-011 dual harm streams, SD-015 z_resource, and MECH-269 per-stream V_s. Together they turn raw environment state into the split latent representations every downstream module consumes.
tour.languageLesson: The stream-separated latent design (z_self vs z_world vs z_harm) is a soft type system encoded through composition rather than Python types: each encoder returns a differently-named tensor so downstream code must consume the intended stream, and the cross-stream binder is the one place they are allowed to mix.

tour.title: E1, E2, and E3 -- Prediction and Selection
tour.description: The predictor stack is the working machinery of the agent's world model. E1 is the long-horizon deep predictor with a 16-slot cue-indexed context bank; E2 is the fast forward model over (z_world, action) plus counterfactual rollouts and predictive-uncertainty heads; E3 is the trajectory selector implementing action selection with precision/authority arbitration and WCI floors. Reading these files reveals how a candidate action becomes a scored trajectory before the beta-gate lets it out.

tour.title: Hippocampus, Anchors, and Ghost Goals
tour.description: The hippocampal module navigates SD-004 action-object space and generates value-flat CEM trajectory proposals under ARC-007. Its anchor set is a scale-tagged episodic store with dual-trace preservation, the event segmenter emits monotonic outer.inner segment IDs, and the ghost-goal bank scores anchors on a wanting+goal_match+staleness+recoverability composite so the residue field can propose 'unfinished business' to bias exploration.

tour.title: The Sleep Cycle and Consolidation
tour.description: Sleep is where offline integration happens in V3. SleepLoopManager drives the deterministic K-episode SD-017 cycle, the replay sampler draws anchors from a frozen staleness/priority snapshot, RoutingGate weights channels per-phase, BayesianAggregator maintains per-domain per-region posteriors over residuals, cross_module_consolidation orchestrates interleaved E1/E2 replay, and the MEL consumer adapts sleep cadence from accumulated Model Error Load. This is one of the substrates most unique to REE-v3.

tour.title: Cingulate and Claustrum -- Salience and Coalitions
tour.description: The SD-032 cingulate cluster produces the agent's control signals: dACC computes precision-weighted affective prediction error and adaptive control, AIC signals interoceptive salience/urgency, pACC integrates sustained affective pain, PCC emits a metastability parameter, and the salience_coordinator fuses them into an operating-mode signal. The SD-091 claustrum sits next to them as a star-topology coalition controller that opens typed control-demand channels (SENSORY_RESAMPLE, PROVENANCE_CHECK, ...) when the salience coordinator asks for reconfiguration.

tour.title: PFC Substrates -- Rules, Escape, and De-Commit
tour.description: The PFC layer hosts the more deliberate control substrates. Lateral PFC (SD-033a) holds MECH-262 rule-selective persistence with mode-conditioned rule-state EMA. Infralimbic PFC (MECH-357/SD-058) suppresses PAG freezing and biases E3 toward escape when appropriate, backed by the escape_affordance_bridge and the post-603i escape-affordance linker over E2. Frontopolar (SD-033e) provides the V4-scope de-commit lever with a V3-narrow deterministic fallback. Together they turn raw score into deliberate action.

tour.title: Regulators, Neuromodulators, and PAG
tour.description: Regulators are pure-arithmetic gain/decay/override modules that shape the substrate without training. GABAergic decay applies cross-stream tonic exponential decay; the broadcast-override regulator emits an orexin-analog signal from sustained drive; serotonin provides tonic-5HT state with benefit/harm salience tagging; the PAG freeze-gate treats freeze as a committed behavioural state with GABAergic-toned commit/exit thresholds. Reading them together shows how V3 separates learned representation from neuromodulatory bias.

tour.title: Amygdala, Affect, and Attribution
tour.description: The affect layer converts moment-by-moment prediction errors into slow, agent-relevant valence. BLA and CeA are non-trainable amygdala analogues consuming z_harm_a; the attribution_head learns to route harm signals to a cause. Blocked-agency (z_block) accumulates the 'assumption of control failure' as a pure-arithmetic regulator, while harm_suffering_accumulator applies hysteretic controllability gating to convert unpleasantness into slow suffering. These are the streams that let residue and dACC treat some episodes as care-marked.

tour.title: Preservation -- Birth Replay and Reconstruction
tour.description: Preservation is REE's answer to the question 'what makes this specific organism recoverable later?'. ReconstructionRecord is an immutable, integrity-hashed bundle of the exact inputs (config, seed, environment, provenance, ...) needed to re-birth an agent bit-identically. The archive backends are content-addressed and append-only, with S3 replication; the physical-token exporter produces an engravable ~180-byte key line plus a gzipped full record for out-of-band preservation. This is what turns an experiment run into something durable.
tour.languageLesson: Content-addressed storage (SHA-based keys) makes an artefact self-verifying: the identifier IS the integrity check, so any tampering is caught at read time. Combined with append-only writes it produces an audit trail that cannot be silently rewritten, which is why REE uses it for the birth-replay preservation layer.

tour.title: Bridge -- The Coordinator Plan of Record
tour.description: V3 is not a solo agent -- every substrate above runs inside experiments whose queue, results, telemetry, and claims are coordinated by a hub service. PLAN.md is the plan-of-record: it explains the rationale (git-as-IPC was becoming a bottleneck), the target end-state (a single-writer coordinator on the hub), the HTTP API contract, the SQLite schema, and the phased/reversible rollout. Read this before diving into app.py or db.py so the design choices there make sense.

tour.title: The Coordinator HTTP API
tour.description: coordinator/app.py is a pure-stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer with bearer-token auth exposing the endpoints the fleet talks to: claim arbitration (/claim), the chip ledger, heartbeat/status ingest, and the manifest spool. Every worker in the fleet POSTs its results and heartbeats here rather than committing to git directly -- app.py is the choke point that turns concurrent workers into a serialisable stream of intents.

tour.title: SQLite Persistence -- The Schema That Serialises the Fleet
tour.description: coordinator/db.py wraps a SQLite database that is the authoritative source of truth for the queue, results, heartbeats, claims, chips, and workspace-state spools. It uses WAL and a BEGIN IMMEDIATE around every claim guard so claim arbitration is atomic even under concurrent /claim requests. The tables shown here (experiments, results, heartbeats, task_claims, chip_ledger, workspace_state_entries, git_intent_log) are the exact shapes the sync_daemon materialises into git in the next step.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite in WAL mode with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` gives you a lightweight single-writer transactional store without a server. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` grabs the write lock at transaction start rather than lazily on first write, which is how coordinator/db.py serialises claim arbitration: the losing session's guard read and insert happen inside one exclusive lock, so racing /claim POSTs deterministically resolve to a single winner.

tour.title: The Sole-Writer Sync Daemon and Materializers
tour.description: sync_daemon is the only process on the hub that commits coordination-data files to git -- runners never touch REE_assembly or ree-v3 directly. Phase 1 reads git to reconcile the DB (a shadow soak); Phase 3 authoritative writers materialise result manifests, queue snapshots, and heartbeat/status files from the DB into the two repos. task_claim_chip_git_writer is the twin materialiser for TASK_CLAIMS.json / TASK_CHIPS.json / WORKSPACE_STATE.md / decision-log JSONL. This is why the CLAUDE.md coordination-rules exist: they encode what the sync_daemon owns.

tour.title: Operating the Coordinator in Production
tour.description: The OPERATOR_GUIDE and PHASE3_CUTOVER docs close the tour by showing how everything above runs in the real fleet: the Explorer coordination panel, the three-system architecture (git + coordinator API + sync_daemon writers), the five-phase cutover checklist, hub telemetry transport, the queue-writer conflict-recovery, and the daemon knobs. The SOAK_LOG records how Phase 1 shadow observations converged with git reality before the cutover -- it is the evidence that made the Phase 3 flip safe.
